relevance_note: Case series of 15 infantile Alexander disease patients with per-patient GFAP mutations in Table 1: 'Missense, heterozygous, de novo GFAP mutations were found in exons 1 or 4 for 14 of the 15 patients analyzed'.
method_note: Read the paper in full; a Python script (own scratch dir) transcribed Table 1 (15 present-study patients) and Table 2 (rows marked * = patients of Brenner et al.) cell by cell, and the output was checked against both tables by eye. Labels: present-study patients are 'patient N' (the text uses 'patient N'); Table 2 rows marked with an asterisk are 'Table 2 #N*' (bare index with the table's asterisk), except Brenner patient 11*, whom the text calls 'patient 11 of Brenner et al. [2001]' (rule 1). The asterisk's meaning is inferred from the Table 2 title and that sentence; the Table 2 footnotes (a, b, c) and Table 1 footnotes a-c are missing from the converted text, so Head circumference, Seizures (+/++/+++), Macrocephaly '-' and '0', and Severity symbols have no legend: '-' and '0' were treated as not reported, '…' as not reported, and the Table 1 seizure/head-circumference cells were not used (seizures and macrocephaly come from the text). Table 2 '+' in the Macrocephaly column was taken as observed for Brenner patient 6*. Ages: Table 1 onset and delay columns are in months (header '(mo)'); status column in years. Deceased ages for patients 12 and 14 come from the text (53 mo; 15 mo) rather than Table 1 (4.5 y; 1.2 y). Table 2 'Disease Duration' was not recorded as an age. Variants: Table 1 nucleotide changes are printed without 'c.' and with the arrow converted to 'r' (e.g. 240CrT); recorded exactly as printed. Missense and heterozygous come from statements covering the 14 patients with detected mutations. De novo only where Table 1 shows '2 nl' (both parents normal, footnote e); patient 13 '1 nl' and patients 1, 4, 6, 9 left not reported despite the general statement 'In all patients analyzed, the GFAP mutations are dominant and arise de novo'. Brenner patients' zygosity/inheritance/type left not reported (the Brenner group statement covers '10 of 11' cases, not clearly these 13 rows). Time-limited absences ('None had spasticity or ataxia until age 18 mo') were recorded as excluded feature rows with detail 'until age 18 mo' but left not reported in the checklist; 'only one had a progressive macrocephaly' excludes only progressive macrocephaly (narrower) for patients 2, 9, 13. White matter abnormality for the eight milder patients comes from the sentence on why the diagnosis was suspected in them (group statement). Contradictions: (1) text says the patient without a GFAP mutation was 'patient 10 of the present work', but Tables 1 and 2 give patient 15 'None' and patient 10 R239C; I followed the tables and did not use that sentence for patient 10 or 15. (2) Patient 12 death at 53 mo (text) vs 4.5 years (Table 1). (3) Brenner R79 patients: text gives alive ages 7 and 8 years, but Table 2 disease durations for the alive R79 Brenner patients are 12 and 6 years; no ages were assigned to Brenner R79 patients. Abstract says 'four had R239C' consistent with Table 1 (patients 10-13).
